findings.current: For unorthodox martial artists already living in the Central Plains, though, things were different.
findings.defect: The translation omits the source’s description of the Central Plains as the center of the world, a detail preserved in the accepted baseline.
findings.rationale: The Korean explicitly describes the Central Plains as the central region of the world (천하의 중심부).
findings.replacement: For unorthodox martial artists already living in the Central Plains—the very heart of the world—things were different.

findings.current: The Hidden Shadow Pavilion, led by Sir Song, the Thousand-Faced Fox, also kept them under close watch.
findings.defect: “Close watch” weakens the source’s explicit description of the Pavilion’s surveillance as ironclad.
findings.rationale: 철통같은 감시 describes exceptionally tight, ironclad surveillance; the accepted baseline preserved that degree of scrutiny.
findings.replacement: The Hidden Shadow Pavilion, led by Sir Song, the Thousand-Faced Fox, also kept them under ironclad surveillance.

summary: The assembled English is broadly faithful. Two minor source details were weakened or omitted: the Central Plains’ description as the heart of the world, and the ironclad nature of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s surveillance.
